content.title: Stages of management of patients with acute heart failure
content.caption_note: ICCU = intensive coronary care unit; ICU = intensive care unit

Immediate: Limit organ damage (cardiac, renal, hepatic, gut)
Pre-discharge and long-term: Improve symptoms and quality of life

Immediate: Close monitoring of vital signs and grading severity of symptoms/signs
Initial treatment to support circulatory and respiratory functions (vasodilators, vasopressors, inotropes, diuretics, supplemental O2)
Intermediate: Identify aetiology and relevant co-morbidities and start targeted treatment
Titrate therapy to control symptoms and to relieve congestion, manage hypoperfusion and optimize blood pressure
Initiate and up-titrate disease-modifying pharmacological therapy
Consider device therapy in appropriate patients
Pre-discharge and long-term: Initiate and up-titrate disease-modifying pharmacological and device therapy
Develop a care plan with identification of caregivers, a schedule for up-titration and monitoring of pharmacological therapy, review of device therapy
Enrollment in a disease management programme

management_flow_summary.urgent_phase: After first medical contact: identify cardiogenic shock and/or respiratory failure; provide pharmacological support, ventilatory support, or mechanical circulatory support (MCS) as needed
management_flow_summary.identification_of_acute_aetiology: Immediate identification of cause to enable specific treatment
management_flow_summary.next_steps: Immediate initiation of specific treatment once aetiology identified; proceed to further treatment and ongoing care
